methodologyNotes: Dataset covers 12 benchtop/consumer ultrasonic cleaners spanning budget jewelry cleaners through professional/lab-grade baths, the range a 2026 buyer actually compares. Seed list was verified against manufacturer and specialist-retailer pages; two seeds could not be substantiated as real, current, US-market products and were corrected: 'LifeBasis 2.5L' does not exist in LifeBasis's current lineup (their largest tank is 750-850 ml) and was replaced with their verified flagship, the CD-2820 (750 ml); 'InvisiClean IC-6-Pro' is not a documented model number and was replaced with InvisiClean's actual flagship personal cleaner, the Pro Elite IC-2755 (brand now also sold as VisiClean). 'Ultra 8051E' (James Products Ltd / JPL, UK) was dropped entirely -- JPL stopped manufacturing ultrasonic cleaners in 2021 and the unit was 220-240V-only UK stock, never sold in the US, so it fails the 'a 2026 buyer compares' bar -- and replaced with Elmasonic S30H (Elma, Germany), a genuinely current professional/lab-tier cleaner distributed in the US. The roster was also expanded with L&R Quantrex 140 (a US jewelry/watch-trade industry-standard brand) to properly represent the professional tier. Two entries (CO-Z DUC-1002-00 and CREWORKS DUC-M02J-US) rely on cross-referenced retailer/marketplace listings rather than a successfully loaded manufacturer page, because cozpalace.com and creworksequipment.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt during this research session; their specs are corroborated across at least two independent listings each (eBay, DealNews, and the identical-SKU sister-brand page) and are flagged as lower-confidence in each product's provenance field. VEVOR's own site geo-redirected every request to vevor.fr and then 404'd, so its spec figures are drawn from VEVOR's own indexed listing title/description text rather than a live-rendered page; its price is left null rather than guessed. Fields that could not be verified from any accessible source are null rather than estimated, per the 'null beats a guess' rule -- this affects several ultrasonic_power_w/heater_watt splits (many listings only publish combined wattage) and most releaseDate values (none of these ongoing product lines had a documented launch year on any accessed page). tank_capacity_l is the manufacturer-stated nominal tank volume in liters. ultrasonic_power_w and heater_watt are reported separately where the manufacturer publishes them separately; where only a combined 'total power' figure exists, that is noted in provenance rather than split by guesswork. All accessedAt 2026-08-01.

products.name: Branson CPX-952-116R (Bransonic M1800) Ultrasonic Cleaning Bath
products.priceNote: Sale price at ultrasoniccleaners.com; list price shown as $696.00. Industrial/lab distributor pricing varies by channel.
products.provenance: Verified on an authorized Branson (Emerson) distributor product page. This 0.5-gallon 'M'-size model has no heating element (explicitly stated). The 90W figure is the unit's rated power draw at 0.8A, not necessarily an ultrasonic-only figure -- Branson does not publish a separate ultrasonic-only wattage for this model. Mechanical control, no digital display. Sweep-frequency technology is used to eliminate standing waves.

products.provenance: SEED SUBSTITUTION: the requested seed 'Ultra 8051E' is a James Products Ltd (JPL) unit, UK-manufactured, 220-240V only, and JPL stopped producing ultrasonic cleaners entirely in 2021 -- it was never sold in the US and is no longer available new anywhere, so it fails the brief's 'a buyer compares in 2026' bar. Replaced with Elmasonic S30H (Elma, Germany), a genuinely current professional/lab-tier cleaner distributed in the US (e.g. via Cole-Parmer and lab suppliers), representing the premium tier a buyer would realistically cross-shop against Branson. Power figures: Elma publishes 280W total system power at 220/240V for the non-US-voltage S30(H) family; a separate ultrasonic-only/heater-only split for the US 120V unit could not be confirmed, so both are left null rather than estimated.
